meta.author: lbernick
meta.body:
It may be helpful to rephrase the chart in terms of actions a user needs to take:
- If you want default behavior of coschedule-workspaces, no action needed
- If you were already disabling the affinity assistant, no action needed now, but at some point you'll need to set `coscheduling` to `disabled`.

For Andrea's proposal:
- If you were previously accepting default behavior but now want one of the new features, just set `coscheduling` to the value you want
- If you were previously disabling the affinity assistant but want one of the new features, you need to set `disable-affinity-assistant` back to "false" and then turn on the new behavior.

For Quan's original proposal:
- If you were previously accepting default behavior but now want one of the new features, you need to  set `disable-affinity-assistant` to "true" and then turn on the new behavior.
- If you were previously disabling the affinity assistant but want one of the new features,  just set `coscheduling` to the value you want.


I personally find Quan's original proposal less confusing, but I am open to either. The two most important things IMO are:
1. Preserving existing behavior for users setting "disable-affinity-assistant" to "true" (which both of these proposals do)
2. Including the chart in our docs

meta.body:
I think we still need to call APIs to delete `pvcs` at `pr` completion/deletion time anyways. 

The advantage of this approach is that there is no extra work to delete the `pvcs` at `pr` deletion time, as the owner of the `pvcs` are the `prs` not the `aa statefulset` (i.e. k8s automatically deletes the pvcs when the owning prs are deleted). 

In addition, this patch fully reverts the pvcs behaviours in 1 pull request. If we just revert the highlighted part but not merge the followup prs in one release, users will still see the different behavior (i.e. `pvcs` are not deleted when `pr` is deleted). 

I personally feel this full revert could be a better solution. I'm open to the partial solution if we can make sure to merge all the followup prs in one pr, but I don't see much advantage.
